review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

6:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν, καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
6:1.targetText: Jesus went on from there and came to His hometown, accompanied by His disciples.

groups.note: BSB recasts "His disciples follow Him" as "accompanied by His disciples".

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed in English.
The dative object αὐτῷ (Him) is absorbed by the recast "accompanied by".
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the verb ending.

6:2.sourceText: καὶ γενομένου σαββάτου ἤρξατο διδάσκειν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ· καὶ οἱ πολλοὶ ἀκούοντες ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες Πόθεν τούτῳ ταῦτα, καὶ τίς ἡ σοφία ἡ δοθεῖσα τούτῳ; καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τοιαῦται διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ γινόμεναι;
6:2.targetText: When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished. “Where did this man get these ideas?” they asked. “What is this wisdom He has been given? And how can He perform such miracles?

groups.note: The genitive absolute γενομένου σαββάτου supplies the temporal clause.
The article before σοφία is rendered with demonstrative force.
Dative τούτῳ "to this one" becomes the subject of the English passive.
διὰ τῶν χειρῶν … γινόμεναι "being done through the hands" is recast as the active "perform".
Genitive αὐτοῦ "his (hands)" becomes the subject of "perform".

unmappedSource.reason: Opening connective is not separately expressed.
Connective not separately expressed in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for "heard".
English supplies a question auxiliary; the Greek question is verbless.
English supplies the verb; Πόθεν τούτῳ ταῦτα has no verb.
English supplies the copula.
English supplies "how can"; the Greek question has no interrogative word or modal verb.

6:3.sourceText: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τέκτων, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς Μαρίας καὶ ἀδελφὸς Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσῆτος καὶ Ἰούδα καὶ Σίμωνος; καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ ὧδε πρὸς ἡμᾶς; καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ.
6:3.targetText: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well?” And they took offense at Him.

groups.note: οὐχ … ἐστιν "is not" together form the contraction.
οὐκ εἰσίν "are not" together form the contraction.

unmappedSource.reason: English lists these names with commas instead of these conjunctions.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:4.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
6:4.targetText: Then Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”

groups.note: Οὐκ … εἰ μή "not … except" is rendered as fronted "Only".

unmappedSource.reason: Recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech is not rendered.
English uses a comma instead of this conjunction.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:5.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἐδύνατο ἐκεῖ ποιῆσαι οὐδεμίαν δύναμιν, εἰ μὴ ὀλίγοις ἀρρώστοις ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐθεράπευσεν.
6:5.targetText: So He could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐπιθείς and the main verb with "and"; no Greek καί.
English supplies the object of "heal".

6:6.sourceText: καὶ ἐθαύμασεν διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν. Καὶ περιῆγεν τὰς κώμας κύκλῳ διδάσκων.
6:6.targetText: And He was amazed at their unbelief.  And He went around from village to village, teaching the people.

groups.note: The publisher's Greek has a different form of the same verb θαυμάζω.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for "teaching".

6:7.sourceText: Καὶ προσκαλεῖται τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοὺς ἀποστέλλειν δύο δύο, καὶ ἐδίδου αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν ἀκαθάρτων,
6:7.targetText: Then Jesus called the Twelve to Him and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.

groups.note: The middle προσκαλεῖται means "called to Himself".
The genitive πνευμάτων "of the spirits" is rendered "over … spirits".

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed; BSB renders the next verb as the participle "giving".
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the verb ending.

6:8.sourceText: καὶ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδὲν αἴρωσιν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰ μὴ ῥάβδον μόνον, μὴ ἄρτον, μὴ πήραν, μὴ εἰς τὴν ζώνην χαλκόν,
6:8.targetText: He instructed them to take nothing but a staff for the journey—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts—

groups.note: εἰ μή "except" is rendered "but".

unmappedSource.reason: Opening connective is not separately expressed.
μόνον "only" is absorbed by "nothing but".

6:9.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ὑποδεδεμένους σανδάλια, καὶ μὴ ἐνδύσησθε δύο χιτῶνας.
6:9.targetText: and to wear sandals, but not a second tunic.

unmappedSource.reason: English does not repeat a verb here; "not a second tunic" relies on the earlier "to wear".

6:10.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθητε εἰς οἰκίαν, ἐκεῖ μένετε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε ἐκεῖθεν.
6:10.targetText: And He told them, “When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area.

groups.note: Ὅπου ἐάν "wherever" is rendered "When".

unmappedSource.reason: The preposition εἰς is absorbed by the transitive English "enter".

6:11.sourceText: καὶ ὃς ἂν τόπος μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσωσιν ὑμῶν, ἐκπορευόμενοι ἐκεῖθεν ἐκτινάξατε τὸν χοῦν τὸν ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
6:11.targetText: If anyone will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place, as a testimony against them.”

groups.note: ὃς ἄν "whichever (place)" is rendered as the condition "If anyone".

unmappedSource.reason: Opening connective is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:12.targetText: So they set out and preached that the people should repent.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐξελθόντες and the main verb with "and"; no Greek καί.
English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

6:13.sourceText: καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλλον, καὶ ἤλειφον ἐλαίῳ πολλοὺς ἀρρώστους καὶ ἐθεράπευον.
6:13.targetText: They also drove out many demons and healed many of the sick, anointing them with oil.

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed; BSB renders the anointing verb as a participle.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of "anointing".

6:14.sourceText: Καὶ ἤκουσεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης, φανερὸν γὰρ ἐγένετο τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάνης ὁ Βαπτίζων ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐνεργοῦσιν αἱ δυνάμεις ἐν αὐτῷ.
6:14.targetText: Now King Herod heard about this, for Jesus’ name had become well known, and people were saying, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”

groups.note: Genitive αὐτοῦ "his" is rendered with the name.
Same name; the publisher's Greek spells it Ἰωάννης.
Article and participle ὁ Βαπτίζων "the one baptizing" form one title.
διὰ τοῦτο "because of this" is rendered "That is why".

unmappedSource.reason: Recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech is not rendered.
Connective not separately expressed in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for "heard".
English supplies the copula in "That is why".

6:15.sourceText: ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἡλείας ἐστίν· ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι προφήτης ὡς εἷς τῶν προφητῶν.
6:15.targetText: Others were saying, “He is Elijah,” and still others, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old.”

groups.note: Same name; the publisher's Greek spells it Ἠλίας.

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed in English.
Recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech is not rendered.
The second "were saying" is left implicit in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek clause is verbless.
English adds "of old"; no Greek word.

6:16.sourceText: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἔλεγεν Ὃν ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα Ἰωάνην, οὗτος ἠγέρθη.
6:16.targetText: But when Herod heard this, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead!”

groups.note: Same name; the publisher's Greek spells it Ἰωάννην.

unmappedSource.reason: The resumptive οὗτος "this one" is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for "heard".
English adds "from the dead" from 6:14; the Greek has only ἠγέρθη.

6:17.sourceText: Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἀποστείλας ἐκράτησεν τὸν Ἰωάνην καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν ἐν φυλακῇ διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι αὐτὴν ἐγάμησεν·
6:17.targetText: For Herod himself had ordered that John be arrested and bound and imprisoned, on account of his brother Philip’s wife Herodias, whom Herod had married.

groups.note: The participle ἀποστείλας "having sent" is rendered "had ordered".
Same name; the publisher's Greek spells it Ἰωάννην.
ἐν φυλακῇ "in prison" is rendered by the verb "imprisoned".

unmappedSource.reason: The object pronoun αὐτόν is not repeated in the English passive series.
Causal ὅτι "because" is recast as the relative clause "whom … had married".
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies "and" when it turns "bound him in prison" into "bound and imprisoned".
English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

6:18.sourceText: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάνης τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ ὅτι Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
6:18.targetText: For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!”

groups.note: Same name; the publisher's Greek spells it Ἰωάννης.

unmappedSource.reason: Recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:19.sourceText: ἡ δὲ Ἡρῳδιὰς ἐνεῖχεν αὐτῷ καὶ ἤθελεν αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο·
6:19.targetText: So Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him. But she had been unable,

groups.note: Dative αὐτῷ "against him" is rendered with the name.
οὐκ ἠδύνατο "was not able" is rendered by the single word "unable".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:20.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης ἐφοβεῖτο τὸν Ἰωάνην, εἰδὼς αὐτὸν ἄνδρα δίκαιον καὶ ἅγιον, καὶ συνετήρει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀκούσας αὐτοῦ πολλὰ ἠπόρει, καὶ ἡδέως αὐτοῦ ἤκουεν.
6:20.targetText: because Herod feared John and protected him, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man. When he heard John’s words, he was greatly perplexed; yet he listened to him gladly.

groups.note: Same name; the publisher's Greek spells it Ἰωάννην.
Genitive αὐτοῦ "him" (the one heard) is rendered "John’s".

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed; BSB begins a new sentence.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in "knowing that he was"; the Greek has αὐτὸν ἄνδρα δίκαιον "him a righteous man".
English supplies "words" as what was heard; the Greek says "hearing him".

6:21.sourceText: Καὶ γενομένης ἡμέρας εὐκαίρου ὅτε Ἡρῴδης τοῖς γενεσίοις αὐτοῦ δεῖπνον ἐποίησεν τοῖς μεγιστᾶσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῖς χιλιάρχοις καὶ τοῖς πρώτοις τῆς Γαλιλαίας,
6:21.targetText: On Herod’s birthday, her opportunity arose. Herod held a banquet for his nobles and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.

groups.note: ἡμέρας εὐκαίρου "an opportune day" is rendered "opportunity".
The temporal dative τοῖς γενεσίοις supplies "On".
Genitive αὐτοῦ "his" is rendered with the name.
The dative τοῖς μεγιστᾶσιν supplies "for".

unmappedSource.reason: Opening connective is not separately expressed.
ὅτε "when" is not rendered; BSB starts a new sentence.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessor (Herodias); no Greek pronoun.

6:22.sourceText: καὶ εἰσελθούσης τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος καὶ ὀρχησαμένης, ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ καὶ τοῖς συνανακειμένοις. ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τῷ κορασίῳ Αἴτησόν με ὃ ἐὰν θέλῃς, καὶ δώσω σοι·
6:22.targetText: When the daughter of Herodias came and danced, she pleased Herod and his guests, and the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.”

groups.note: The genitive absolute εἰσελθούσης … ὀρχησαμένης supplies the temporal clause.
τοῖς συνανακειμένοις "those reclining with (him)" is rendered "his guests".
The dative τῷ κορασίῳ supplies "to".

unmappedSource.reason: Opening connective is not separately expressed.
The intensive αὐτῆς "herself" is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for "give".

6:23.sourceText: καὶ ὤμοσεν αὐτῇ Ὅτι ἐάν με αἰτήσῃς δώσω σοι ἕως ἡμίσους τῆς βασιλείας μου.
6:23.targetText: And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom!”

groups.note: Ὅτι ἐάν (read ὅ τι ἐάν) "whatever" is rendered "Whatever".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:24.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσα εἶπεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς Τί αἰτήσωμαι; ἡ δὲ εἶπεν Τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάνου τοῦ Βαπτίζοντος.
6:24.targetText: Then she went out and asked her mother, “What should I request?”  And her mother answered, “The head of John the Baptist.”

groups.note: In ἡ δέ "and she" the article is a pronoun; BSB names the mother.
Same name; the publisher's Greek spells it Ἰωάννου.
Article and participle τοῦ Βαπτίζοντος "the one baptizing" form one title.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐξελθοῦσα and the main verb with "and"; no Greek καί.

6:25.sourceText: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσα εὐθὺς μετὰ σπουδῆς πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα ᾐτήσατο λέγουσα Θέλω ἵνα ἐξαυτῆς δῷς μοι ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάνου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ.
6:25.targetText: At once the girl hurried back to the king with her request: “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately.”

groups.note: εἰσελθοῦσα μετὰ σπουδῆς "going in with haste" is rendered "hurried back".
ἵνα with the subjunctive is rendered as an English infinitive.
Same name; the publisher's Greek spells it Ἰωάννου.

unmappedSource.reason: Opening connective is not separately expressed.
The participle λέγουσα "saying" is not rendered; BSB introduces the words with a colon.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the feminine participle.

6:26.sourceText: καὶ περίλυπος γενόμενος ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς ἀνακειμένους οὐκ ἠθέλησεν ἀθετῆσαι αὐτήν.
6:26.targetText: The king was consumed with sorrow, but because of his oaths and his guests, he did not want to refuse her.

groups.note: The opening καί is rendered as the contrast after "consumed with sorrow".
τοὺς ἀνακειμένους "those reclining (at table)" is rendered "his guests".

6:27.sourceText: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀποστείλας ὁ βασιλεὺς σπεκουλάτορα ἐπέταξεν ἐνέγκαι τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.
6:27.targetText: So without delay, the king commanded that John’s head be brought in. He sent an executioner, who went and beheaded him in the prison.

groups.note: Genitive αὐτοῦ "his" is rendered with the name.
BSB ends its 6:27 with the first clause of Greek 6:28; καί is recast as the relative "who".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀπελθών and the main verb with "and"; no Greek καί.

6:28.sourceText: καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπεκεφάλισεν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ, καὶ ἤνεγκεν τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῷ κορασίῳ, καὶ τὸ κοράσιον ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς.
6:28.targetText: The man brought John’s head on a platter and presented it to the girl, who gave it to her mother.

groups.note: Genitive αὐτοῦ "his" is rendered with the name.
The dative τῷ κορασίῳ supplies "to".
καὶ τὸ κοράσιον "and the girl" is recast as the relative "who".
The dative τῇ μητρί supplies "to".

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed at the start of the BSB verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject (the executioner); the Greek has only the verb ending.

sourceMoved.reason: BSB places "who went and beheaded him in the prison" at the end of its 6:27.

6:29.sourceText: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦλθαν καὶ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔθηκαν αὐτὸ ἐν μνημείῳ.
6:29.targetText: When John’s disciples heard about this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.

groups.note: Genitive αὐτοῦ "his" is rendered with the name.
The publisher's Greek has another form of the same verb (ἦλθον).

unmappedSource.reason: Opening connective is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for "heard".

6:30.sourceText: Καὶ συνάγονται οἱ ἀπόστολοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησαν καὶ ὅσα ἐδίδαξαν.
6:30.targetText: Meanwhile, the apostles gathered around Jesus and brought Him news of all they had done and taught.

groups.note: πάντα ὅσα "all that" is rendered "all".

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated relative ὅσα is not rendered in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:31.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Δεῦτε ὑμεῖς αὐτοὶ κατ’ ἰδίαν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον καὶ ἀναπαύσασθε ὀλίγον. ἦσαν γὰρ οἱ ἐρχόμενοι καὶ οἱ ὑπάγοντες πολλοί, καὶ οὐδὲ φαγεῖν εὐκαίρουν.
6:31.targetText: And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.

groups.note: κατ’ ἰδίαν "by yourselves" is an idiom for "privately".
The plural imperative "rest" is rendered "let us rest".

unmappedSource.reason: The emphatic ὑμεῖς αὐτοί "you yourselves" is not rendered; BSB recasts the invitation as "Come with Me".

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies "with Me"; no Greek word.

6:32.sourceText: καὶ ἀπῆλθον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατ’ ἰδίαν.
6:32.targetText: So they went away in a boat by themselves to a solitary place.

groups.note: κατ’ ἰδίαν "privately" is an idiom.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:33.sourceText: καὶ εἶδον αὐτοὺς ὑπάγοντας καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν πολλοί, καὶ πεζῇ ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν πόλεων συνέδραμον ἐκεῖ καὶ προῆλθον αὐτούς.
6:33.targetText: But many people saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before them.

unmappedSource.reason: Connective not separately expressed; BSB begins a new sentence.
ἐκεῖ "there" is not separately rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for "recognized".

6:34.sourceText: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον, καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὅτι ἦσαν ὡς πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα, καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς πολλά.
6:34.targetText: When Jesus stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.

groups.note: The participle ἐξελθών "having gone out" supplies the temporal clause.
μὴ ἔχοντα "not having" is rendered "without".

Connective not separately expressed in English.

6:35.sourceText: Καὶ ἤδη ὥρας πολλῆς γενομένης προσελθόντες αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος, καὶ ἤδη ὥρα πολλή·
6:35.targetText: By now the hour was already late. So the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late.

groups.note: The opening καί is rendered at the main clause.
ἤδη "already" is rendered twice, "By now … already".
Dative αὐτῷ "to Him" is rendered with the name.

Recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech is not rendered.

6:36.sourceText: ἀπόλυσον αὐτούς, ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τοὺς κύκλῳ ἀγροὺς καὶ κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς τί φάγωσιν.
6:36.targetText: Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
